title: In Vitro Differentiation of Human CD4+FOXP3+ Induced Regulatory T Cells (iTregs) from Naïve CD4+ T Cells Using a TGF-β-containing Protocol.
markdown:
## Protocol: In vitro induction of regulatory T cells from naïve human CD4-positive T cells using TGF-beta and interleukin-2

### Overview

This protocol details the in vitro induction of regulatory T cells (Tregs) from naïve human CD4-positive T cells using TGF-beta and interleukin-2. The process involves preparation of reagents, isolation of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), separation of natural Tregs (nTregs) and naïve CD4+ T cells, and subsequent culture of naïve cells under specific conditions to induce induced Tregs (iTregs). Key factors include TGF-β1, IL-2, ATRA, rapamycin, or sodium butyrate.

### Materials/Reagents

Ficoll density centrifugation medium; Human serum albumin (or bovine albumin); EDTA; PBS; Serum-free hematopoietic medium; L-alanyl-L-glutamine; Interleukin-2 (IL-2); Acetic acid (100 mM); TGF-β1 (carrier-free powder); HCl (4 mM); All-trans retinoic acid (ATRA); DMSO; Rapamycin; Sodium butyrate; Ultra-pure sterile water; Anti-CD3 antibody; Trypan blue; Naïve CD4+ T Cell Biotin-Antibody Cocktail II; Anti-biotin microbeads; CD25 magnetic beads; RPMI/10% FCS medium; T cell culture medium.

### Equipment

50 ml tubes; 15 ml tubes; 0.5 ml low-protein binding tubes; T175 cell culture flasks; 96-well plates (U-shaped preferred); Centrifuge (capable of room temperature and 4 °C operation, without brake); Magnetic separation system with LS columns; Automatic or manual cell counter; 40 µm cell strainer; Light microscope (40X magnification); Parafilm; Aluminum foil.

### Safety & Sterility

Maintain sterility throughout all procedures involving cell culture and reagent preparation. Use sterile-filtered solutions where specified (e.g., acetic acid, HCl, sodium butyrate). Handle biological samples (blood/buffy coat) according to standard biosafety guidelines. Protect light-sensitive reagents (ATRA, TGF-β1 aliquots) from light and heat. Store sensitive reagents at appropriate temperatures (-80 °C, -20 °C, or 4 °C as specified).

## Reagent Preparation

### Preparation

1. Pre-lay 15 ml of density centrifugation medium (such as Ficoll) into 50 ml tubes (prepare 5 tubes per buffy coat). Pre-warm these tubes to room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. Prepare isolation buffer containing 0.5% (w/v) human serum albumin and 2 mM EDTA in PBS. Keep the buffer at 4 °C at all times. Alternatively, bovine albumin may be used instead of human albumin. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->
3. Prepare T cell culture medium consisting of serum-free hematopoietic medium supplemented with 2 mM L-alanyl-L-glutamine. Pre-warm the medium before use. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S03 -->
4. Prepare an IL-2 stock solution at a concentration of 400,000 IU/ml in sterile-filtered (using an acid-resistant filter) 100 mM acetic acid. If the activity of the lot is 2,400 IU per 1 µg, this corresponds to 167 µg/ml; confirm the activity with the provider. Aliquot the solution into sterilized low-protein binding 0.5 ml tubes, seal with Parafilm, freeze on dry ice, and store at -80 °C for long-term storage or at -20 °C for up to 3 months. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S04 -->
5. Prepare a TGF-β1 stock solution (for a 10 µg carrier-free vial): Centrifuge the TGF-β1 powder at 1,000 x g for 3 minutes. Add 100 µl of sterile-filtered (using an acid-resistant filter) 4 mM HCl to create a stock solution with a concentration of 100 µg/ml. Allow the powder to dissolve completely and vortex. Aliquot 5 µl each into sterilized low-protein binding 0.5 ml tubes, seal with Parafilm, freeze on dry ice, and store at -80 °C for up to 6 months. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S05 -->
6. Prepare an ATRA stock solution by dissolving the powder at 20 mg/ml (66.6 mM) in DMSO. Further dilute in DMSO to prepare a 10 mM stock solution. Aliquot and store protected from light at -80 °C for up to 1 year. Note that ATRA is sensitive to light, heat, and air. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S06 -->
7. Prepare a rapamycin stock solution at 1 mg/ml (1.11 mM) in DMSO. Store in aliquots at -80 °C for up to 1 year. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S07 -->
8. Prepare a sodium butyrate stock solution at 0.908 M (0.1 mg/ml) in sterile ultra-pure H2O. Sterile filter the solution. Aliquot and store at -20 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S08 -->
9. On the previous day, coat plates with anti-CD3 antibody. Coat the desired number of wells in a 96-well plate with 65 µl/well of 5 µg/ml anti-CD3 antibody in PBS. Wrap the plate with foil and incubate overnight at 4 °C. Do not use the margin wells of the 96-well plate. Larger wells may be used, but U-shaped wells facilitate consistent cell numbers per area across experiments. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S09 -->

## PBMC Isolation

### PBMC Isolation

1. Fill up the buffy coat with phosphate buffered saline (PBS) at room temperature. If fresh blood is used, dilute it with an equal volume of PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->
2. Tilt the tube to the side and slowly overlay the density centrifugation medium with approximately 35 ml of diluted blood per tube. Add the blood very carefully to avoid any mixing between the density centrifugation medium phase and the blood layer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->
3. Centrifuge for 20 minutes at 1,150 x g at room temperature without using the brake. Operate the centrifuge without the brake and, if possible, with low to medium acceleration to prevent mixing of the layers. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S03 -->
4. Extract the white ring containing PBMCs located between the density centrifugation medium and the plasma phase. Transfer this material to a new 50 ml tube (perform one transfer with a 5 ml pipette and two transfers with a 2 ml plastic Pasteur pipette). Take as little plasma and density centrifugation medium as possible. Do not touch the red erythrocyte pellet. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S04 -->
5. Transfer the cells to a T175 cell culture flask for adherent suspension. Keep the cells in the original 50 ml tubes (use 2 tubes per buffy coat). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S05 -->
6. Incubate the cells in the laying flask for 45 to 90 minutes at 37 °C with 5% CO2. This step depletes monocytes via plastic adherence. While not mandatory, it increases the percentage of T cell yield relative to the amount of PBMCs in subsequent steps. The tubes can be reused to rinse further columns. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S06 -->
7. Resuspend the cells (contained in the 50 ml medium in the flask) and rinse the cell layer on the bottom of the flask well. Distribute the cells equally into two 50 ml tubes (the previous tubes may be reused for the same donor). Rinse the flask with 50 ml of fresh RPMI/10% FCS medium and transfer equally into the same two tubes. Always wait until the column has stopped dripping before adding any new liquid. Store the flow-through at 4 °C for later steps. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S07 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note: PBMCs may be stored overnight at 4 °C with tubes laid on their side, or ideally, they should be used directly for T cell isolation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S08 -->

## nTreg Isolation

### nTreg Isolation

1. Resuspend and count PBMCs using an automatic or manual cell counter in the presence of trypan blue. Do not count small platelets. If cell clumps are observed, strain the cells through a 40 µm cell strainer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S01 -->
2. Centrifuge the PBMCs at 450 x g for 10 minutes at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S02 -->
3. Resuspend the cells (using a 1 ml pipette) in 90 µl of isolation buffer per 10^7 PBMCs to obtain a single cell suspension. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S03 -->
4. Add 2 µl of CD25 beads per 10^7 cells, mix, and incubate for 15 minutes at 4 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S04 -->
5. Fill the tube with PBS to a total volume of 30 ml. Centrifuge at 450 x g for 10 minutes at 4 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S05 -->
6. Prepare LS columns (use 2 columns per buffy coat): equilibrate each with 3 ml of isolation buffer and discard the flow-through. The tubes can be reused to rinse further columns. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S06 -->
7. Resuspend the cells in 3 ml of isolation buffer per tube (using a 1 ml pipette). Transfer the cells to the LS column and collect the flow-through in fresh 15 ml tubes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S07 -->
8. Rinse the 50 ml tubes with 2 ml of Isolation buffer each. Transfer the rinsing buffer to the columns. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S08 -->
9. Wash each column 2 times with 3 ml of Isolation buffer each. Always wait until the column has stopped dripping before adding any new liquid. Store the flow-through at 4 °C for later steps. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S09 -->
10. Remove the column from the magnet. Elute 2 times with 3 ml of isolation buffer per column into a 15 ml tube. Note: The eluate from 2 columns per donor can be combined. Do not dip the column into the liquid. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S10 -->
11. Prepare and equilibrate new LS columns (use 1 column per buffy coat). Transfer the eluate from the previous step to the column. The flow-through can be discarded. After the eluate has passed through the column, rinse the tube and wash the column 3 times with 3 ml of isolation buffer. Note: The second column is crucially needed to increase purity. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S11 -->
12. Remove the column from the magnet. Elute the CD25++ "nTregs" 2 times with 3 ml of Isolation buffer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S12 -->
13. Centrifuge at 450 x g for 10 minutes at 4 °C. Remove the supernatant completely. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S13 -->
14. Wash the cells with 15 ml of T cell culture medium, centrifuge at 450 x g for 10 minutes at 4 °C, and remove the supernatant completely. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S14 -->
15. Resuspend the cells in 0.5 ml of T cell culture medium supplemented with 100 IU/ml IL-2 each. Transfer the cells to a 24-well plate. Rinse the tube with 0.5 ml of medium (+ 100 IU/ml IL-2) and combine into the 24-well plate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S15 -->
16. Adjust the density of Tregs to 1-2 x 10^6 cells/ml using T cell culture medium + 100 IU/ml IL-2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S17 -->
17. Incubate the Tregs at 37 °C with 5% CO2 until use. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S18 -->

## Naïve CD4+ T Cell Isolation

### Naïve CD4+ T Cell Isolation

1. Combine 2 tubes per donor of Treg-depleted PBMCs in a 50 ml tube. Fill with PBS to 50 ml at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S01 -->
2. Centrifuge the PBMCs at 200 x g for 5-10 minutes at room temperature. Remove and discard the supernatant. Resuspend the cells in 50 ml PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S02 -->
3. Repeat step 1.3.2 twice. NOTE: The PBS washes are crucial for removal of platelets, which will not be removed with the column. Platelet depletion can be monitored in the individual steps on a microscopic slide. The steps have to be performed with PBS and centrifugations at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S03 -->
4. Resuspend PBMCs in 50 ml PBS. Count cells as in step 1.2.2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S04 -->
5. Centrifuge the PBMCs at 450 x g for 10 minutes at 4 °C. Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cells in 40 µl of Isolation buffer (kept at 4 °C) per 10^7 cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S05 -->
6. Add 10 µl of Naïve CD4+ T Cell Biotin-Antibody Cocktail II per 10^7 cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S06 -->
7. Mix the solution and incubate for 10 minutes at 4 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S07 -->
8. Wash the cells by adding 40 ml of PBS (kept at 4 °C), and centrifuge at 450 x g for 10 minutes at 4 °C. Remove the supernatant and resuspend the cells in 80 µl of isolation buffer per 10^7 cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S08 -->
9. Add 20 µl of anti-biotin microbeads per 10^7 cells. Mix well and incubate for 15 minutes at 4 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S09 -->
10. Fill to 50 ml with cold PBS, and centrifuge at 450 x g for 10 minutes at 4 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S10 -->
11. Prepare LS columns (equilibrate with 3 ml of isolation buffer). To avoid column overload, use one column for a maximum of 250 x 10^6 PBMCs, or less if the PBMCs contain many red blood cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S11 -->
12. Remove the supernatant and resuspend the cells in 3 ml of isolation buffer. Transfer the cells to the LS column. Collect the flow-through, which contains the naïve CD4+ T cells, in 15 ml tubes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S12 -->
13. Rinse the tube with 2 ml of isolation buffer. Transfer to the following negative isolation kit. Platelets remain in the supernatant at this low-speed centrifugation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S13 -->
14. Wash the column 3 times with 3 ml of isolation buffer. Always wait until the column stops dripping before adding any new liquid. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S14 -->
15. Take the flow-through (naïve CD4+ T cells) and an unstained sample for flow cytometry settings and compensation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S15 -->
16. Centrifuge at 450 x g for 10 minutes at 4 °C. Columns can be discarded. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S16 -->
17. Remove the supernatant completely. Wash the cells with 15 ml of medium, centrifuge at 450 x g for 10 minutes at room temperature, and remove the supernatant completely. Note: Isolation buffer contains EDTA, which chelates calcium ions and thus impairs T cell activation. Before any stimulation assays, remove the isolation buffer completely and wash the cells twice with 15 ml of medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S17 -->
18. Resuspend the cells in T cell culture medium to a density of 2-3 x 10^6 cells per ml. Rest the cells in an appropriate flask or well overnight in the incubator. If the cells are used directly for stimulation assays, wash them one more time with medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S18 -->

## Treg Induction Culture

### Day 0: Plating

1. Prepare 4x concentrated premixes (50 µl per well) in T cell culture medium as specified in Table 1. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S01 -->
2. For each well, add 50 µl of 4x anti-CD28/IL-2 premix (add T cell culture medium instead for "unstimulated" cells), 50 µl of 4x TGF-β1 premix, and either 50 µl of 4x ATRA/rapamycin or butyrate premix (where applicable) or medium. For "stimulation only" mock controls, add 50 µl of T cell culture medium instead of the ATRA/rapamycin/butyrate premix. Protect ATRA from heat and air. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S02 -->
3. Fill all empty wells, including the margin wells, with 200 µl of PBS. Pre-warm the plates at 37 °C with 5% CO2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S03 -->
4. After resting the cells, transfer them to a 15 ml tube. Rinse the flask/wells with pre-warmed T cell culture medium and pool the contents into the tube. Fill the tube to 15 ml with T cell culture medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S04 -->
5. Centrifuge the cells at 450 x g for 10 minutes at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S05 -->
6. Remove medium and take up cells in fresh, prewarmed T cell culture medium to a density of 2.2-2.6 x 10^6/ml. Count cells as in step 1.2.2 and adjust density if needed. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S06 -->
7. Add cells to prepared stimulation plates (see 2.1), 50 µl cells/well (110,000-130,000 cells/well). Each well sample should now contain a total volume of 200 µl. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S07 -->
8. Wrap the plates in aluminum foil to protect ATRA from light. Incubate at 37 °C with 5% CO2 for the desired time periods. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S08 -->

### Day 2-3: Monitoring

1. Monitor Treg cultures by light microscopy at 40X magnification. From about day 2 to 3, small clusters of proliferating cells should become visible, which merge into bigger clusters at later time points. Cultures grown with rapamycin generally show less growth. See also Figure 3. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T1-S01 -->

### Culture Duration

1. At desired time points, take samples for RNA extraction or flow cytometry phenotyping. For later time points with cell proliferation, 1 well each is sufficient. Otherwise, take 1 x 10^5-1 x 10^6 cells each for RNA and 3 x 10^5-1 x 10^6 cells for flow cytometry. Note: This protocol is optimized for staining in a 96U well plate format with 3 x 10^5-1 x 10^6 cells. If there are fewer cells per well, start with several wells and pool as described below. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T2-S01 -->
2. Extract RNA and perform qRT-PCR for FOXP3 and a housekeeping gene (such as RPL13A) according to standard protocols. In addition, measure the expression of other Treg signature genes (for example, 'Treg up' genes IL2RA, CTLA4, IKZF4, and 'Treg down' genes IFNG, SATB1). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T2-S02 -->
3. Remove the remaining supernatant completely from the cells. Proceed directly to RNA extraction or freeze the cell pellet on dry ice and store at -20 °C to -80 °C for up to 2 weeks. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T2-S03 -->
